question: Find the area of a triangle whose base is 28 cm and corresponding altiude is 15 cm.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The area of a triangle can be directly calculated when the base and height are known using the direct formula.

⇒ Area = 1/2 × base × altitude

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 28 × 15

⇒ Area = 14 × 15 = 210 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 210 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Base of the triangle (b) = 28 cm

⇒ Corresponding altitude (h) = 15 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Area of a Triangle = 1/2 × b × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 28 × 15

⇒ Area = 14 × 15

⇒ Area = 210 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 210 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Heron's Formula

Used when all three side lengths (a, b, c) are known: Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

Area of an Equilateral Triangle

For a triangle with all three equal sides of length a: Area = (√3 ÷ 4) × a².

Area of a Right-Angled Triangle

When the base and perpendicular are explicitly given forming a right angle: Area = 1/2 × Base × Perpendicular.
